case.amplicon_range_bp: 490 bp for the insertion (I) allele, 190 bp for the deletion (D) allele; an intermediate heteroduplex band is also reported in heterozygotes
case.caveats: Template substitution: the paper cites EMBL X62855 as the sequence it worked from, but X62855.1 is only 1856 bp and stops 36 bp short of the reverse-primer site (the forward primer matches at 1403 and the I-allele amplicon would run 1403..1892), so X62855 cannot serve as the template. AF118569.1 was substituted and does carry the insertion allele. Size discrepancy: 490/190 are gel estimates and are internally inconsistent with the paper's own 287-bp Alu; the sequence-derived lengths on AF118569.1 are 480 bp (filled, at 14044..14523) and 193 bp (empty). expected_amplicon_bp is reported as the paper's 490, not the measured 480. Text-layer note: the PDF renders the sense oligo as 'CTGGAGACCACTCCCATCC1TT-CT'; the '1' is an OCR artifact for T, confirmed by the exact single-site genomic match at the ACE intron 16 locus. Both primers have exactly one site on AF118569.1.
case.citation: Rigat B, Hubert C, Corvol P, Soubrier F. PCR detection of the insertion/deletion polymorphism of the human angiotensin converting enzyme gene (DCP1) (dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase 1). Nucleic Acids Res. 1992;20(6):1433. doi:10.1093/nar/20.6.1433-a. PMID 1313972; PMCID PMC312213.
case.element: Alu element (SINE), 287 bp, inserted in intron 16 of the ACE/DCP1 gene at 17q23
case.loci_justification: The pair flanks one locus on the cited template: a single insertion site, a single excision site, or a single transcript. A second product on this template would be an off-target prediction.
case.name: Human ACE (DCP1) intron 16 Alu insertion/deletion polymorphism (the classic ACE I/D assay)
case.where_in_paper: The 'PCR Conditions' paragraph gives both oligos verbatim; the sentence immediately after states 'The PCR product is a 190 bp fragment in the absence of the insertion and a 490 bp fragment in the presence of the insertion.'
case.worked_prediction_note: The entry records a worked prediction — a coordinate range, an in-silico check, or a sequence-derived length — so the expected answer was written down before the engine ran. The published size remains external, but this case was not scored blind.
